bybit_extension_condition: Activate Bybit only after an official pre-IPO contract and an official timestamp method are bound to the immutable plan.
objective: Test whether a paper LONG or SHORT entered on a pre-IPO perpetual can produce executable net economics around an official equity IPO or conversion event.
hypothesis: A pre-IPO perpetual may offer an executable event-relative LONG or SHORT before IPO price discovery, but basis, rebase, funding, queue and conversion risk can erase the apparent edge.

provenance.reason: bitmex and kraken promoted from candidate to active collection. Both publish a per-instrument launch timestamp on a public unauthenticated endpoint - BitMEX `listing`, Kraken `openingDate` - and both now have adapters that classify from the declared equity list rather than guessing, because neither venue publishes a pre-IPO marker. Neither timestamp is an observed first trade, so neither can satisfy exact_first_trade_t0; both map to tradable_ts. Promotion is safe to do before either venue has answered because a failing venue is isolated to its own RETRY_NEXT_INTERVAL outcome and cannot break collection from okx and gate. cryptocom and coinbase_intx stay candidates: their instrument response shapes could not be confirmed from documentation, and a normaliser written against guessed field names would silently mis-map data.

Temporal anchors separated. The collectors collapsed an announced spot t0, a transition and a contract launch into one event_eta_utc with an or-chain, then asserted exact_timestamp from the contract record's source_class alone - dropping the second half of the test the model already carried in has_official_listing_time. Anchor selection filtered only on a timestamp being present, called the result 'upcoming', sorted ascending and took the first, which on a set holding past events pins the stalest one permanently. official_confirmed and exact_timestamp were any() across the batch, attaching one contract's official source to another contract's timestamp. And decide_cadence had no time check on its CONFIRMED branch, so a confirmed anchor held the hourly cadence forever. Measured 2026-08-24: the crypto track reported CONFIRMED against an event_eta of 2025-09-01 and the pre-IPO track against 2026-05-07, both asserting official_confirmation=True. The plan already required official_and_proxy_separate and proxy_cannot_escalate_to_confirmed; the code did not honour it.

technical_rebind.reason: Rebind current fail-closed launchers, retry recovery and canonical writer controls without changing venue, universe, signal, cost, risk, cadence or acceptance contracts.

temporal_anchor_contract.rule: the kind of moment stays attached to the moment; only an official_spot_t0 published by an official source may claim an exact official time, and every other kind is a proxy that the cadence policy already refuses to escalate
temporal_anchor_contract.source_class_is_not_timestamp_class: source_class describes where the contract record came from, not where its timestamp came from; the two were conflated
temporal_anchor_contract.anchor_selection: the earliest still-future anchor among live contracts; with nothing ahead, the freshest past anchor, which the cadence policy then retires on its own age
temporal_anchor_contract.confirmation_scope: official_confirmed and exact_timestamp are properties of the selected anchor, never any() across the batch
temporal_anchor_contract.measured: 2026-08-24: preipo official_conversion_ts is read from Bybit preMktSwTime and OKX conversion_time, which the hardened capture repo maps to transition_ts and refuses official_spot_t0 without an OFFICIAL_ANNOUNCEMENT; no venue endpoint feeding the pre-IPO track publishes a spot t0, so that track carries no exact official time at all

acceptance_gate_change.reason: A verdict was wanted sooner. Lowering minimum_complete_events would have delivered that and destroyed the verdict: at n=10 with profit_factor >= 1.2 a single good event carries the whole statistic, so 'accepted' would stop meaning anything. The acceptance threshold therefore does not move. An interim tier at 10 reports the same metrics early under INSUFFICIENT_DATA_NOT_REJECTED and is structurally unable to authorise: interim_authorizes is False and the validator requires interim_descriptive_events to sit strictly below minimum_complete_events, so the two tiers cannot be collapsed into one by later raising the interim number.
